root_idea.summary: The root centers on severity, force, and sharpness, especially a forceful or harsh quality.
root_idea.development: This orientation appears in harsh temperament, vehemence and strength, abundance or intensity, and the overwhelming rush of water. Terms for variegated coloring are treated as anomalous or possibly involving substitution, while the male-rat interpretation of the Quranic expression is disputed.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The Quranic noun is displayed under the normalized citation form عَرِمٌ.

senses.definition: A dam or embankment raised across a valley or torrent-bed.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic expression سَيْلُ الْعَرِمِ, this is the interpretation in which the barrier was breached and the flood followed.

senses.definition: An overwhelming torrent or violent, devastating rain.
senses.usage_conditions: This is an alternative interpretation of the Quranic expression, emphasizing the force and intractability of the water rather than a dam.
Reported as an interpretation of the Quranic expression on the explanation that the animal bored through the dam and thereby caused the flood.

senses.definition: A proper name for a valley in Yemen.
senses.usage_conditions: Reported as another interpretation of the noun in the Quranic passage; the supplied evidence does not establish a more specific modern location.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be harsh, ill-natured, perverse, sharp, vehement, or strong in disposition.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a child or man; the same verb is also reported with the sense of becoming bad, corrupt, or wicked.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be ignorant.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An alternative lexical use of the Form I verb.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a bone, to exhale its scent or odor, especially when burnt.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The form and sense are specifically stated of a bone.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To treat someone with ill-natured harshness or extreme perversity.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A transitive construction with a person as object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To strip flesh from a bone with the front teeth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A transitive construction involving eating the flesh from a bone.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of camels, to crop trees or obtain pasture from them.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of animals feeding by taking material from trees.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a child, to suck the breast of its mother.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A transitive construction may take the mother or her breast as its object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Mixing one thing with another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The Form II construction عَرَّمَهُ بِهِ means that he mixed one thing with another.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Contending in an altercation, disputing, or litigating, and thereby causing conflict or discord.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reciprocal or interpersonal construction, synonymous with contention and quarrelling.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To induce someone to commit an evil deed that he had not previously committed.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A transitive Form IV causative construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The becoming hard to bear, severe, or distressing, especially of trials, conflicts, or factions.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used with فِتَن and related situations of conflict or hardship.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a mare, to go at random or headlong, disregard guidance, and deviate from the right course.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The usage is specifically reported of a mare.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a mother, to seek a breast-feeding infant; alternatively, to draw milk from her own breasts and expel it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The cited expression also received figurative explanations involving undertaking an irrelevant task or censuring oneself when no target is available.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Grease, gravy, or dripping exuded from meat and fat; also the residue or dirt of a cooking-pot.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The word can denote either the edible dripping or the remains adhering to the pot.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Variegation or speckling produced by black mixed with white; also a mixed collection of sheep and goats.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The coloration may occur in an animal's coat, lip, or ear; the livestock sense denotes a collection containing both sheep and goats.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An iron helmet.
A quantity or heap of reaped grain, especially wheat or barley, collected and trodden for winnowing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: It may denote grain not yet winnowed or grain that has subsequently been winnowed.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A place where sand collects.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The plural is reported as عَرَمَاتٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A heap of dung.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This sense is reported as an alternative explanation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Flesh-meat, especially the meat of a slaughtered camel.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in an expression describing meat as savory.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The odor of cooked flesh-meat.
A vineyard.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An uncommon, attributed lexical report.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Evilness of disposition, ill-nature, perversity, or repugnance.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The noun may describe a person; in related usage it includes annoyance or molestation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Sharpness, force, vehemence, or vigorous abundance.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: It may describe a beverage, an army's force and numerousness, or another strongly manifested quality.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Quitting the right course and exceeding proper bounds.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative or behavioral extension of the quality of forceful excess.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Ignorance.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A separately reported nominal use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The flesh clinging to a bone, or material stripped or cropped from a tree, including its bark.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The tree sense may refer specifically to bark or to portions taken by browsing animals.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A calamity or misfortune.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The word is connected with the hardness or pressure of the event.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Relating to ignorance or characterized by ignorance.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A relational adjective derived from the reported sense of عُرَامٌ as ignorance.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Ill-natured, perverse, repugnant, insolent, unthankful, bad, corrupt, or wicked.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied especially to a child or man; its feminine plural is also used as an epithet of irritating creeping insects. أَعْرَمُ expresses a higher degree of the same quality.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Sharp, vehement, or strong.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The adjective can qualify a tongue or another forceful manifestation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Ignorant.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A separately reported adjectival use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Extremely or vehemently cold.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a day or night; the plural expression refers to vehemently cold nights.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A suckling at the breast, or the act of sucking the breast.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The word may denote either the nursing child or the associated action in the cited usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Hard, strong, or vehement; also numerous, especially when applied to an army.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The adjective can be applied broadly to things, while the army sense emphasizes massed strength or number.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a man, having a strong degree of difficulty or barbarousness in speech.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized description of defective or non-Arabic utterance.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Speckled or marked with black and white; two-coloured or variegated.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to sand-grouse eggs, a serpent, or a sheep or goat with a white mark or black specks; it may also describe a mixed flock of sheep and goats.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Uncircumcised.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used as an epithet of men; reported plurals include عُرْمَانٌ and عَرَامِينُ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A tiller or cultivator of land.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Reported as a singular of عُرْمَانٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A place or tract of seed-produce.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Reported as a plural usage associated with places producing grain or seed.

cautions: The single Quranic occurrence occurs in سَيْلُ الْعَرِمِ, a phrase with competing interpretations: dam, overwhelming torrent or rain, male rat or gerbil, and a valley name. The supplied contextual gloss selects the dam interpretation but does not settle the exegetical alternatives.

The male-rat interpretation is reported in Quran-focused lexical evidence but is rejected in the supplied root-level discussion; it is therefore retained as a reported Quranic interpretation, not presented as certain.
